items.location: body: Probiotics and live biotherapeutic products
items.note: Lactobacillus plantarum: safety confirmed but no GVHD outcome result yet (trial ongoing). [129,130]

items.quote: It highlights key metabolites, the bacterial taxa that produce them and the substrates involved in their synthesis
items.location: table 1
items.note: Table 1 lists metabolite-producer taxa; the GVHD link is taxon->metabolite->GVHD (via the metabolite's therapeutic potential), not a direct taxon->GVHD association. Codebook question: should producer taxa become 1a/1b/1c protective rows?

items.quote: Trials were chosen based on methodical rigour, prioritizing those with prospective, randomized and controlled designs when possible
items.location: table 2
items.note: Table 2 is intervention-level (trial -> GVHD outcome) with no microbial-target->GVHD claim beyond the prose already captured (HERACLES butyrate producers / pathobionts).

items.quote: Bacteria are associated with favourable effects (blue clades) or unfavourable outcomes (red clades) following allogeneic haematopoietic cell transplantation
items.location: figure 2
items.note: Fig 2 labels carry only a collective caption citation (refs 15-21,24,31,39,40,42,44,66,127,181-185), not per-label citations, so rule 2 excludes them. Several taxa appear only here (Thomasclavelia, Actinomycetaceae, Lachnoclostridium, Oscillospiraceae with directions, Bacteroidota/MAIT); promote with the collective refs if wanted.

items.quote: In GVHD, dysbiosis and impaired microbial metabolism result in reduced production of these protective metabolites, contributing to epithelial cell damage and immune dysregulation
items.location: figure 3
items.note: Fig 3 is a mechanism schematic (producer taxa -> metabolites -> barrier/immune) repeating the text and Table 1; caption cites only [186,187]. No per-taxon GVHD citation.
